inputs.text: What stands out is that this policy treats justice as something that depends on who the defendant is. Making execution the default for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis is not equal accountability; it is a starkly unequal use of state power. Protecting victims matters, but expanding the state’s power to kill will not make justice fair or keep all civilians safe. A system that claims to uphold the law must protect everyone’s rights and apply it without discrimination. Outside criticism should be taken seriously when such grave questions of equality and human rights are at stake.

output.main_topic: Execution as the default penalty for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis and its implications for equal justice
